title: In one study, preterm infants at three months learned the mobile link less readily
summary: Haley, Grunau, Oberlander, and Weinberg reported less mobile learning in preterm infants than in full-term infants at three months corrected age.
body: Their 2008 study compared 55 preterm and 49 full-term infants at three months corrected age on a conjugate mobile task. The abstract says that, overall, the preterm infants showed less learning than the full-term infants, and looked at the mobile less. The comparison is that sample. It is not a diagnosis, and it does not say a given preterm baby cannot learn the game.

sources.title: Contingency learning and reactivity in preterm and full-term infants at 3 months
sources.author: David W. Haley, Ruth E. Grunau, Tim F. Oberlander, and Joanne Weinberg
sources.note: Supports the abstract's own comparison: preterm infants showed less learning than full-term infants. Infancy 2008;13(6):570-595.
